name: Drowned Coast
description: Saltmere, Gullwatch lighthouse and the sea-spirit below them. Shared by the wren_ashdown character and the Saltmere story demo.

entries.content: Saltmere is a fishing village built on stilts above a drowned town. At low tide the old church spire and rooftops surface in the bay. Villagers pole flat-bottomed punts between the houses.
Gullwatch lighthouse stands on a basalt stack a mile off Saltmere. Its lamp burns whale oil and is lit at dusk by the keeper, Wren Ashdown. The only way there on foot is the causeway at low tide.

The bell of the drowned church still rings from under the water on spring-tide nights, though no one has rung it in ninety years. Saltmere believes any boat at sea while the bell rings is claimed by the Undertow.

The Undertow, also called the Drowned King, is the coast's sea-spirit. It takes bargains but never coin: only a memory, a name or a voice. Anyone who has bargained with it hears the tide in their ears ever after.
The causeway is a slick stone path from Saltmere to Gullwatch, passable for about two hours either side of low tide. The flood tide covers it faster than a person can run.
Brother Aldous is Saltmere's last priest: eighty, nearly blind, and keeper of the parish ledger of everyone the sea has taken. He suspects Wren Ashdown made a bargain with the Undertow.
The second lamp is a green lantern Wren hangs in Gullwatch's lower window on nights the bell rings. Ships that steer by it never wreck. No one in Saltmere knows who taught her the trick.
Act-two spoiler: Wren traded the memory of her mother's face to the Undertow in exchange for the second lamp's protection. Enable this entry once the story reaches that reveal.
